O Brahmins, what is the use of much speaking regarding Śiva’s status as the object of worship? Śiva, the bringer of auspiciousness, is to be meditated upon.
Abandoning any deity other than Śiva for the sake of worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 18 ||
(In the Skanda Purāṇa, in the dialogue between Vyāsa and Viṣṇu: He sought refuge in the god Śaṅkara with his whole being.
Having abandoned all others, including Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the rest, like blades of grass.
(In the Saurasaṃhitā: Having abandoned all the gods, one should worship the five-faced Lord.
Abandoning all other mantras, one should always recite the five-syllabled mantra. (From the *Brahmagītā*)
Through devotion to Viṣṇu and through devotion to me, there is no higher goal—there is none, indeed.
"It is indeed the truth that I have declared: for all [beings], it is solely through devotion to Śambhu. — From the Kālikākhaṇḍa.
O Lord of All, like parrots, we exist solely for Your sport.
By Your opening and closing of the eyes, our dissolution and emergence occur.
(From the Sūtasaṃhitā:

Therefore, for the destruction of all inauspiciousness, one should joyfully and constantly recite the name beginning with "Nārāyaṇa," having abandoned the supreme terms such as "Mahādeva" and "Śiva," and remaining ever-vigilant. || 23 ||
In the Śāmbhava Purāṇa.
Indeed, names such as Nārāyaṇa and others do not produce direct perception.
To know these names is the fruit of even a small amount of austerity. || 24 ||
In the Parāśara Purāṇa:
Nārāyaṇa, Hari, Viṣṇu, Mukunda, Keśava, and Acyuta.
Names such as these are certainly not concerned with ultimate reality.
Even though they are recited in the proximity of the instruction on the supreme reality, [they do not lead to liberation].
Words function in some way through figurative application; they do not [apply] in their primary sense.
By all the names beginning with Viṣṇu and Nārāyaṇa as well.
The supreme state is not described by what is stated in the Śruti, Smṛti, and Purāṇas.
In the Mānava Purāṇa:
Having thoroughly investigated and abandoned names such as Nārāyaṇa and others.
One who desires immediate liberation should chant the names of Śiva and the others. || 28 ||
The etymological derivation of the names Nārāyaṇa and others is found in the Kāraṇāgama.
The waters are Nārāyaṇa, Rudra, and the Puruṣa who is dark-brown.
Therefore, the waters indeed come into being; thus he is remembered as Nārāyaṇa.
In the Skanda Purāṇa:
The waters are called *nārāḥ*, for *nārāḥ* are indeed the offspring of *nara*.
Because he is their place of rest, he himself is called Nārāyaṇa.
And likewise in the Liṅga Purāṇa:
"We have heard that 'the waters are the offspring of man' are the names of the waters."
For he filled his own course with them.
Because he rests within the waters, he is therefore renowned as Vāsudeva.
In the Śivarahasya.
At the end of a thousand divine years, from the womb of that wise one...
For I am Adhokṣaja, having emerged from the lower gate.
Names such as these indeed have the supreme reality as their ultimate referent.
Therefore, those [states] do not exist; hence, they should not be recollected by those seeking liberation.
In the Vāyavyasaṃhitā:
The description of Śiva as the object of worship:
having abandoned minor deities through action, mind, and speech.
Worship that very Lord Īśāna, accompanied by Sāmba, with a heart full of devotion. || 33 ||
In the Parāśara Purāṇa:
Having abandoned the god Śaṅkara (having abandoned the Lord Īśāna together with Umā), they worship another deity.
Deluded, they fall into this most terrible cycle of existence.
Those who, having abandoned the Lord Śambhu, worship others for the sake of liberation—
Overcome by that great darkness, they do not attain the supreme goal.

In the *Tātparya-saṃgraha*, it is stated that the divinity of the Lord within the host of gods, as well as His status as a Brahmin and the object of worship for Brahmā, are established by the *Prapada-mantra*.

"You are a Brāhmaṇa; therefore, one must seek refuge in you alone. Other than you, O Brāhmaṇa, no others are to be worshipped by us. Indeed, it is only through service to the best of the twice-born that we are worthy of honor; our own tradition is the authority for this. (36)
For there is a mantra known as the *prapada*, well-known in the Sāmaveda, which is as follows: [Śruti].
"You are a Brahmin among the Vedas; I am a Brahmin among men. Indeed, a Brahmin seeks refuge with a Brahmin"—in this regard, it is stated in the Parāśara Purāṇa.
Therefore, the connection with a Brahmin is indeed honored by Śiva himself.
The Saṃkaras were all the gods, while Purandara was the Vṛṣala. || 37 ||
The Grandfather (Brahmā) would be a Vaiśya, while Hari is the supreme Kṣatriya.
The Blessed One Rudra is a Brāhmaṇa, the highest of the high among all.
For Rudra’s state of being Brahman, his status as a Brāhmaṇa, is not born of any cause.
Indeed, in this world, a Brahmin always seeks refuge with a Brahmin. || 39 ||
One should take refuge in Mahābrahmā, the Lord, and not in others.
The best of the twice-born [saw] himself as the great Virūpākṣa at all times.
(In this matter, according to the Vātula-tantra:)
Rudra alone is always directly the Brāhmaṇa by virtue of his nature as Brahman.
Since he was recited by the Brāhmaṇas, Rudra is indeed the Brāhmaṇa himself.
The king is the protector of his subjects; Viṣṇu is the protector of the universe.
Therefore, King Hari [concluded] that his Brahminhood was merely figurative.
And the unborn Blessed One has a task at hand regarding the expansion of the world.
It would belong to a Vaiśya alone, and not to a king nor to the best of the twice-born. || 43 ||
Tryambaka, the destroyer of Tripura, is the king of kings over all.
All his followers, headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, [were likewise present].
Therefore, for Brahmins, their own deity, the Great Brahmin Rudra alone, is to be worshipped.
In the Yajurveda.
He who indeed sacrifices by bypassing his own deity.
He falls away from his own deity; he does not reach the further shore and becomes worse off.
(From the Śivasaṃkalpopaniṣad: Brahmā is higher than the highest; Hari is higher than that which is higher than the highest.
But the Lord is higher than that which is higher; may my mind be intent upon Śiva’s resolve. (From another Purāṇa.)
O believers, Brahmā arose from Prajāpati, and Viṣṇu arose from Brahmā.
Even Viṣṇu is surpassed by Hara; therefore, Maheśvara is the Great One in person.

One should offer salutations at the pair of divine, glorious lotus feet of Śrī Mahādeva, the Supreme beyond the supreme, who is established by the authority of numerous scriptural statements from the Vedas, Purāṇas, and Āgamas, such as those declaring Him to be the object of worship for Śiva.

It should not be performed for others. When it is asked, "How so? [the answer is given in the Taittirīya Yajur-Āraṇyaka]: "To whom there is obeisance—that is the head; Dharma is the crown; Brahma is the upper jaw; Viṣṇu, the sacrifice, is this year; the two Aśvins are the generative organ."
The two fore-feet are Atri and Madhyama; the two hind-feet are Mitra and Varuṇa; Agni is the first section of the tail;
then Indra, then Prajāpati, and the fourth is Fearlessness (*abhaya*) at the junction;
the divine Śākvara is the porpoise (*śiṃśumāra*). (In the Ṛgveda: "Praise the famous one, who sits upon the chariot-seat, the youthful..."

O Rudra, who art fierce, terrible, and a slayer of the enemy, be gracious to the singer when praised; let thy hosts descend upon another than this man. (In this regard, it is stated in the Skanda Purāṇa.)
Having meditated upon the *prāṇaliṅga* within the mind, he himself performs that very worship.
Therefore, worship performed with the purity of the three instruments is prescribed. || 46 ||
According to such scriptural and traditional authorities as these, Śiva alone is the one who is to be meditated upon and worshipped.
Those who worship Viṣṇu and others are inferior; they are not to be looked upon, nor are they to be spoken with.

Furthermore, having realized that Śiva alone is eternal and the liberator from all bonds, while the deities headed by Hari have been consumed by the fire of the cycle of birth and death (saṃsāra), the Śruti sought refuge in the Supreme Lord, the ocean of compassion. When it is asked how that occurred, this Śruti says: "Oṃ, the Unborn... [ajāta].

"Thus, O Rudra, some fearful person takes refuge; protect me eternally with that face of yours which is turned to the south. (From the *Āditya Purāṇa*): "By the touch of the dust of whose feet I attained the state of Brahmā, and by whom [the wielder of the Śārṅga bow] also attained the state of Viṣṇu after bearing him upon his head. (47)
In the Sūtasamhitā.
But he who, having abandoned the worship of the Liṅga, worships other deities, [is a transgressor].
Just as a foolish person, having abandoned a jewel, looks for glass. || 48 ||
Brahmins should never speak of the worship of Brahmā or Viṣṇu at any time.
One should constantly worship Rudra and abandon Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
[Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "The Renunciation of Other Deities," in the section on Worship within the *Śrīvīraśaivācārapradīpikā*.]
[Now begins the twelfth chapter.
|| Homage to the venerable gurus.
Now, I shall declare the state of being worshiped by all deities and its fruit. In the Ṛgveda:
O Rudra, the Maruts praise your splendors; for your birth is beautiful and wondrous.
"That supreme step of Viṣṇu which was set down."
In this matter, [it is stated] in the Parāśara Purāṇa: "The Rudra-liṅga of Mahāviṣṇu is made of stone; it is to be kept secret, even from those who are secret."
Having worshipped Cārucitra, he attained the supreme state. || 1 ||
And she is celebrated as Lakṣmī, the beloved of Mahāviṣṇu.
Having worshipped whose linga, she is to be honored by all conscious beings.
Indeed, by the worship of whose linga Brahmā, the creator of the entire world, [attains his status].
He quickly attained the speech that is honored by all conscious beings.
By the very worship of his *liṅga*, even women become beloved by their husbands.
Goddess Śacī and other women are to be honored by all conscious beings. (From the Puruṣasūkta:
By means of sacrifice the gods sacrificed the sacrifice; those were the first dharmas.
Those great ones have attained the firmament where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide.
(From the Śivadharmottara)
Having worshipped whose linga, all the Maruts as well—
They attained full prosperity and became worthy of worship by all conscious beings.
Viṣṇu always worships a liṅga made of sapphire (indranīla).
And by means of this, he attained the state of Viṣṇu, which is eternally one and everlasting.
And so it is stated in the Vāyavīya-saṃhitā:
Then Janārdana, having obtained that status from Maheśvara, was satisfied.
He went to the radiant, delightful, and supreme abode of Vaikuṇṭha.
(In the Liṅga Purāṇa)
And having worshipped his feet with devotion by means of thousands of lotus flowers.
Having worshipped the Supreme Lord, Madhusūdana then offered praise.
And one lotus was lacking from the thousand lotuses.
Mādhava himself worshipped it, having extracted one of his own eyes.
From that time forward, those of virtuous vows called him Padmākṣa.
For that purpose, Nīlalohita gave his eye and his discus to Viṣṇu.
(From the *Skanda Purāṇa*, in the dialogue between Vyāsa and Jaimini)
Brahmā constantly worships an auspicious linga made of stone.
By worshipping him, he attained the supreme state of Brahmahood. || 11 ||
Śakra, the lord of the gods, also [worshipped] the auspicious linga made of jewels.
Because he worshipped him constantly with devotion, he attained the status of Śakra.
Agni worships with devotion that meritorious clay liṅga.
And by this, he attained the state of fire, becoming a blameless manifestation of splendor.
Varuṇa always worships the beautiful linga made of jewels.
By that, he indeed attained that state of Varuṇa, which is the most excellent increase.
The Description of the Fruit of Śiva-worship:
Vāyu constantly worships an auspicious liṅga made of copper.
By that [act], he attained the state of wind, endowed with incomparable qualities.
Dhanada always worships the golden linga with devotion.
By that means, the god Dhanada has always attained the status of the Giver of Wealth.
Ravi always worships that copper linga with devotion.
By worshipping him three times a day, he attained the supreme state of the Sun.
Soma always worships a linga made of pearls.
Through that Soma, he attained the state of being Soma, eternally radiant.
Kandarpa constantly worships the auspicious linga made of flowers.
By that, one always attains the state of Kāma and victory over the three worlds. || 19 ||
The high-souled Viśvedevas [worship] a beautiful silver liṅga.
Those who worship according to the rules with devotion shall thereby attain the state of being the universe.
The Vasus worship a bell-metal linga according to the prescribed rites.
Those great-souled ones shall attain the most enchanting state of the Vasus.
The Aśvins, worshipping the earthly Liṅga according to the prescribed rites, [attained their goal].
By him, first of all, both the twin gods Aśvins, who possess divine bodies, [were honored]. || 22 ||
The Mothers always worship a linga made entirely of iron.
By that means, they shall attain motherhood, which is difficult to obtain in all the worlds.
The foremost among the asuras worship a supreme liṅga made of iron.
And by that, the high-souled Rākṣasas shall attain prowess.
Those Piśācas worship a divine linga made of tin.
Endowed with divine sovereignty, they proceed to the supreme state. || 25 ||
The Guhyakas and others worship a linga made of the three metals.
By that, endowed with the fruit of enjoyments, they go to the supreme state. || 26 ||
The best of serpents worship a linga made of excellent coral.
By that, the nāgas, enriched with great enjoyments, shall attain the supreme state. || 27 ||
In this way, the gods, gandharvas, along with yakṣas, uragas, and rākṣasas—
They worship Īśāna, the leader of the gods, at all times.
[Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Worship of All Deities," in the section on Worship within the Vīraśaivācārapradīpikā.]
[Now begins the thirteenth chapter.
|| Homage to the venerable gurus.
Now, I shall describe the greatness of the worship of the Śiva-liṅga.
(In the Ekapādapurāṇa:
[He beheld] the God of gods, the Teacher of the World, seated upon the peak of Kailāsa.
Resembling the interior of a lotus, with eyes like lotuses and a beautiful face. || 1 ||
It is the supreme destroyer of Time for those bound by the noose of Time.
The supreme Śiva, who possesses all arts, who transcends all arts, and whose form is Time itself.
Kālī herself is the dark digit (kalā), while Gaurī is the beloved one with lotus-like eyes.
Falling at his feet, the goddess Pārvatī spoke with joy.
(Pārvatī said: O Blessed One, Lord of the gods of gods, omniscient Supreme Lord!
O God Maheśvara, I ask this question for the sake of my own welfare.
What fruit can there be from even touching the linga, when it is already attained through its mere sight?
O Śaṅkara, tell me the fruit obtained when a Liṅga is worshipped and praised.
The Lord said:
Excellent, excellent, O highly fortunate one, you who are affectionate toward your devotees!
O beloved, by the sight of the Liṅga, sin indeed goes to destruction.
(Laiṅga): By the sight of the Liṅga in the morning or at night, one dispels sin.
For a living being, [the merit] accumulated from birth until midday, and that performed during the night over seven lifetimes, [is destroyed].
(Likewise, in the Kūrma Purāṇa: On the thirteenth day, at night, one should worship the Three-eyed Lord with offerings.
Having beheld the Lord during the first watch of the night, one is liberated from all sins.
The sin committed over ten million lifetimes is destroyed by the sight of Virūpākṣa.
All that perishes quickly, like a bundle of cotton by fire. || 9 ||
(From another text: Even one who eats what is forbidden to eat, or a killer of a Brahmin, or even a killer of his mother.
A killer of a father, a slayer of a child, a killer of a cow, and a murderer of a woman or a Śūdra. || 10 ||
He speaks of the faults of others and defames the virtues of others.
He was miserly, a speaker of falsehoods, and a thief of precious gems. || 11 ||
O son, even one burdened with all sins is liberated by the sight of the Liṅga.
Recollection of past births, sovereignty, knowledge of the sciences, and the happiness of one's progeny. || 12 ||
Whether out of ignorance or even out of fear, having seen [the Lord], one attains Śaṅkara.
The sight of the Liṅga is meritorious; from seeing it, touching it is auspicious.
In the Śivadharmottara: The Śiva-liṅga is of great merit and is saluted by all the gods.
Even he who touches it with his two hands is not defiled by sins.
(In the dialogue between Umā and Maheśvara:
There is the purification through the ritual assignment (*nyāsa*) of the hands and limbs, as well as the purification of the body.
There shall be constant purity from everything by touching and beholding the Liṅga. || 15 ||
Whether he be a matricide, a patricide, a slayer of a hero, or even a destroyer of an embryo.
Or even one who is uninitiated, by touching Śiva, is liberated from all sins. || 16 ||
The fruit of worshipping Śiva is that, by even a mere touch at all times, one thereafter attains the status of a Gaṇapati.
If one offers it with a spirit of devotion, it will grant liberation; of this there is no doubt.
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the fruit resulting from the worship of the Liṅga.
O Goddess, whatever fruit results from all forms of giving and whatever fruit results from all sacred fords— || 18 ||
Whatever fruit of all sacrifices there is, and whatever merit arises from austerity;
One attains all that in its entirety and prospers in happiness in the hereafter. || 19 ||
By the worship of the Liṅga alone, the destruction of all sins shall occur.
There is no doubt that the fruit of all forms of giving is thereby obtained. || 20 ||
Whatever fruit is obtained by one who has performed ablutions at thousands of millions of sacred fords;
One obtains that fruit when the worship of the Liṅga has been performed. || 21 ||
And whatever sacred fords there are, as well as oceans, lakes, and ponds.
Whatever merit is gained from their bathing, that same merit is obtained by the worship of the Liṅga.
On the summit of Mount Meru, at Prayāga, and at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean.
Austerity was performed in the Himalayas; the fruit of that is the worship of the Liṅga.
Thousands of Cāndrāyaṇa fasts and hundreds of Taptakṛcchra penances.
All vows have been fulfilled once the worship of the Liṅga has been performed.
Of ten million cows and of a hundred million sacrifices, [the merit is equal].
One obtains the fruit of that gift by performing worship even once. || 25 ||
By worshipping the Liṅga even once, human beings go to heaven.
The perfected ones go to the city of Śiva and sport there for imperishable time.
The world of the earth (bhūrloka), the world of the atmosphere (bhuvarloka), the world of heaven (svarloka), and likewise the world of great light (maharloka).
Janas, Tapas, and Satya—these are proclaimed as the seven worlds. || 27 ||
It is declared that by worshipping a linga even once, one attains residence among them.
And by wandering through thousands of millions of births within the various wombs. || 28 ||
When a Liṅga has been worshipped even once, one is liberated from the bonds of saṃsāra.
Indeed, there are truṭis, kalās, nimeṣas, kāṣṭhās, ardhapraharas, and praharas. || 29 ||
Those who worship Mahādeva attain the supreme goal.
Those who, being deluded, do not worship the Liṅga for the sake of fulfilling their desires and securing their welfare, [are lost].
They emerge from and enter into thousands of millions of wombs.
Having enjoyed the fruit of sacrifice in heaven, the donor [experiences] the fruit of dharma.
One who is devoid of the worship of the Liṅga shall be born dwelling in wombs. || 31 ||
And likewise, through the Gāṇapatya [path], liberation certainly does not occur.
And for those devoted to the worship of the Liṅga, there is no birth from a womb.
Terrified by the fear of dwelling in a womb, they were devoted solely to the worship of the Liṅga.
O Goddess, O most beautiful one, these shall become my attendants.
But he who constantly worships the Liṅga, the Lord of the three worlds, [attains the highest state].
He quickly becomes a vessel for the kingdom of heaven and liberation. || 34 ||
Those who desire great enjoyments or the food of the abode of the thirty gods.
They always worship the lotus feet of Hara with devotion. || 35 ||
(Vyāsa said:
"There were delightful mansions and women adorned with playful ornaments."
Wealth indeed, up to the point of complete satisfaction, is the fruit of the rite of Śiva’s worship.
Good fortune, radiant beauty, truthfulness, generosity, and eloquence.
Valor and universal renown are the fruits of the rite of worshiping Śiva.
May there always be the enjoyment of knowledge for both Vyāsa and Kapila.
There shall be the power of giving, which is the fruit of the ritual of Śiva’s worship. || 38 ||
The acquisition of knowledge, wealth, happiness, noble birth, and the fulfillment of one's heart's desires.
Sovereignty, liberation, or even heaven—these are the fruits of the ritual worship of Śiva.
The Siddhiyoga [is found] in the Brahmāṇḍa, in Pātāla, and on the surface of the earth.
He obtains that which is unattainable, which is the fruit of the ritual of worshiping Śiva.
At the gate were indeed rutting elephants and horses with the speed of the wind.
Women with faces like the full moon are the fruit of the ritual of worshiping Śiva.
The creatorship of Brahmā and the crushing of demons by Viṣṇu.
The sovereignty over heaven belonging to Indra is the fruit of the ritual of worshipping Śiva.
And those gods, asuras, and humans who worship Maheśvara.
Having enjoyed abundant pleasures, they go to the supreme goal. || 43 ||
Whoever recites this meritorious Octet of Worship in the presence of Śiva, [shall attain the supreme goal].
He attains the world of Śiva and rejoices together with Śiva. || 44 ||
He who, out of delusion, does not worship the Liṅga, the Lord of the three worlds.
Nor is he a fit vessel for heaven, nor for liberation, nor even for sovereignty. || 45 ||
The Agnihotra rites, the Vedas, and sacrifices accompanied by abundant sacrificial fees—
These are not equal to even a ten-millionth part of the worship of the Śiva-liṅga.
Whoever gives a hundred thousand milch cows to one who has mastered the Vedas,
The merit of one who worships the Liṅga for even a single day is greater than that. || 47 ||
Whatever merit is found in all the Vedas, and whatever fruit is found in all sacrifices;
From that fruit, one obtains ten million times more; there is no doubt in this matter. || 48 ||
Even he who worships Śaṅkara with devotion for a single day, [attains the supreme goal].
Even he goes to the abode of Śiva; how much more so, then, from worshipping many times? || 49 ||
Indeed, that man who should worship [it] constantly, day after day.
